A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–F. The revised layout and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on synthetic and real datasets, including reconstruction, domain adaptation, anomaly detection, and supplementary analyses in Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results on reconstruction, domain adaptation, anomaly detection, and the additional settings examined in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: The linear and nonlinear FCN, CNN, and sparse-AE architectures, reconstruction objective, and training procedures are retained. The separate architecture section describes existing methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic subspace models, single-cell RNA, CelebA, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and MNIST-M scenarios. The image benchmarks emphasized in v3's main text already appeared in v2's Appendix F.3.

E2.justification: The same linear/nonlinear and model-capacity comparisons are retained. No evaluated baseline is added or removed; the additional citations provide background rather than new experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendix A retain the reported train/test allocations, preprocessing, model-size grids, learning rates, training budgets, and evaluation metrics. Remark C.3 introduces an analytical alternative loss without changing an experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The noise, SNR, capacity, domain-shift, overcomplete-AE, denoising, final-ascent, Laplacian-noise, and sparse-AE analyses are retained. Moving CNN panels into the main text does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 5–15 random seeds and curves showing means with ±1 standard error. Appendix A retains the explicit ten-seed counts for the described sweeps.

E6.justification: Matched results retain their values and trends, including the KNN-DAT value of 0.75 in Figure 12 and the reconstruction examples and PSNR values in Figure 37. The CNN results promoted into the main text already appeared in v2's appendix.

T1.justification: The full-rank assumption and central theorem remain unchanged, with Theorem 4.2 renumbered 5.2. New Remark C.3 defines noisy-input, clean-target error and decomposes it into clean reconstruction error and projected noise, showing why this alternative error need not decrease monotonically. This is a bounded theoretical extension.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same principal claims about linear versus nonlinear AEs, model-, epoch-, and sample-wise multiple descents, and implications for reconstruction, domain adaptation, and anomaly detection.

C2.justification: New Section 8 explicitly contrasts supervised learning with the paper's reconstruction setting, including corruption, distribution shift, and capacity allocation. Remark C.3 adds a substantive qualification concerning noisy-input, clean-target evaluation, while the main interpretations of existing experiments remain stable.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the implementation details, data preparation, normalization, hyperparameters, hardware, and computational-time information. Expanded main-text dataset descriptions largely repeat information already supplied in v2. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused references concerning AE dimensionality reduction, biological batch effects, PCA, and CelebA, including Eraslan et al. (2019), Haghverdi et al. (2018), Minka (2000), and Liu et al. (2015). The central positioning relative to previous double-descent studies is retained.

P1.justification: The combined data/architecture section is split, image datasets and CNNs receive explicit subsections, and a Discussion section is added. Dataset explanations, proof exposition, and the conclusion are expanded, while much of the existing narrative is retained.

P2.justification: The main paper switches from two columns to a single-column TMLR layout, with extensive figure relocation and revised plot resolution, labels, axis limits, and legends. Existing CNN panels from v2 Figures 35(a), 38(a), and 39(a) become main-text Figures 3(c), 4(c), and 5(b), with corresponding training panels reorganized in Appendix D.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a useful explanation of why linear-AE monotonicity need not extend to noisy-input, clean-target evaluation, and makes existing CNN evidence easier to find. These improve interpretation and presentation without expanding the empirical foundation. Some stale panel references remain after relocation, such as Figure 35(b) in Appendix E and Figure 39(b) in Appendix F.3, but the net gain in clarity is modestly positive.
